tools.name: platform_workflows
tools.description: [Arch Build] Arch creates and changes projects, agents, tools, configuration, versions, and deployments. Manage node-based workflows end-to-end (Studio API → runtime). Actions: list, get, create, update, publish, execute, create_tool (expose a workflow as a ProjectTool for agent use), delete, list_versions, activate_version, deactivate_version (publish freezes a version; it is not live until activated), list_executions, get_execution (execute returns only an executionId, so poll the run here), approve_step (resolve a human node, which otherwise blocks the run), list_triggers, create_trigger, update_trigger, delete_trigger, fire_trigger and webhook_urls (triggers are managed through these dedicated trigger actions rather than workflow create/update). Create supports every node type: start, end, function, condition, loop, delay, integration, human, data_entry, agent, tool, api. Edge sourceHandle rules: "on_success" for start/function/agent/tool/integration/api/delay/data_entry (+"on_failure" when config.onFailureEnabled); "on_approve"/"on_reject" for human; each condition id + "else" for condition; "on_complete"/"on_failure" for loop. Destructive actions require user approval. Ordinary writes such as create, update, compile, and test require only a stable idempotencyKey. If the server returns MCP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED for a destructive action, ask the user conversationally and retry the identical call with the same idempotency key plus the returned confirmationRequestId and confirmationDecision:"approved". Never invent a request ID or confirmation grant.

workflowId.description: Workflow ID (required for get, publish, execute, delete; optional filter for list_triggers)

workflowType.description: Workflow type for create (defaults to cx_automation)

nodeType.description: Node type: start, end, function, condition, loop, delay, integration, human, data_entry, agent, tool, api

config.description: Per-node configuration. The keys each node type reads: - start: `inputVariables` [{name, type: string|number|boolean|json|array, itemType?, required?, description?, defaultValue?}] — what the Start panel renders and what execution binds. Declaring workflow-level `inputSchema` instead is also accepted; the server fills the other half. - end: `outputMapping` {name: expression} — what the run returns (the canvas key, `EndNodeConfigSchema`). The plural `outputMappings`, and an array of {name, expression} under either key, are equally accepted. - tool: `toolId` AND/OR `toolName` (either is accepted and the server fills the other), `params` {paramName: expression}, `executionMode`. - agent: `agentId` AND/OR `agentName` (either is accepted and the server fills the other), `input` or `message` (the prompt; templates resolve), `timeout` (seconds). OUTPUT SHAPE: `output.agentResponse` (the agent's text), `output.sessionId`, `output.outcome`, `output.sessionEnded` — there is no `output.text`. - condition: `conditions` [{id, label, expression}] where expression is `{{<path>}} <operator> <value>` — e.g. `{{context.steps.Determine_funding_need.output.fundingRequired}} equals true`. Operators: equals, not_equals, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal, less_than, less_than_or_equal, contains, not_contains, is_empty, is_not_empty, matches_regex; the symbols ==, !=, >, >=, <, <= are accepted as aliases, and a bare path without {{ }} is wrapped for you. A lone `{{<path>}}` is judged by truthiness. The right-hand side may itself be a `{{<path>}}`, so `{{a.x}} greater_than_or_equal {{b.y}}` compares two resolved values. This is still NOT JavaScript: `&&`, function calls and arithmetic do not evaluate. The three-part form [{id, label, field, operator, value}] is equally accepted; give a branch one form or the other, never neither. Each id is also an output handle, and `else` always exists. - loop: `collection` (an expression yielding an array), `itemVariable` (read inside the body as {{context.<itemVariable>.<field>}} in templates and context.<itemVariable> in function code). Body nodes carry `parentId` set to the loop node id and chain with on_success edges among themselves; do NOT draw an edge from the loop node to a body node (`loop_body` belongs to the canvas loop_start marker — on a loop node it is an unknown handle and is reported). The last body step leaves on_success unconnected. After the loop, {{context.steps.<loopName>.output.iterationOutputs}} holds one entry per iteration. Each entry is `{index, currentItem, status, output}` — the body result fields are NESTED UNDER `output`, so read `iterationOutputs[].output.<field>` (or `i.output.<field>` inside a `.map`), never `iterationOutputs[].<field>`. That `output` is shaped by `bodyOutputMappings` {name: expression} (or `bodyOutputMapping`) declared ON THE LOOP NODE; without that key it is null for every iteration. Both mistakes are silent: the loop still runs the right number of times, every body step completes, and the summary step collects empty objects. Route on_complete to the next step; a loop with no body iterates over nothing and reports completed. - function: `code` (authored JavaScript, run in a sandbox). OUTPUT CONTRACT: the step output is the set of properties the code assigns on `context` (`context.total = 42` → `output.total`), and a returned plain object is accepted as the output when the code assigned nothing (`return { total: 42 }`). Returning a number, string or array, or reading without writing, yields an empty output. Upstream data: `context.steps.<name>.output.<field>` (bracket form allowed), `context.steps.start.output.<input>`, inside a loop body `context.<itemVariable>`. - integration: `connectorId`, `actionName`, `connectionId`. - api: `method`, `url`, `headers`, `body`. - human: `assignTo` — "everyone", or "specific" plus `assignees` (email addresses); a bare string or string[] is read as the assignee list. `subject` (or `title`) names the task. Routes on the on_approve/on_reject handles. - delay: `duration`, `unit`. Expressions address a previous step by NAME:

parentId.description: Parent loop/container node ID. A loop body node MUST set this to the loop node id — that is how the engine collects the body.

sourceHandle.description: Output handle on the source node. start/function/agent/tool/integration/api/delay/data_entry use "on_success" (+ "on_failure" when config.onFailureEnabled); human uses "on_approve"/"on_reject"; condition uses each condition id + "else"; loop uses "on_complete"/"on_failure". Omit to auto-normalize.

targetHandle.description: Input handle on the target node

inputSchema.description: Workflow input JSON schema (create/update; null clears on update)

outputSchema.description: Workflow output JSON schema (create/update; null clears on update)

confirm.description: Set to true to confirm destructive operations (delete, delete_trigger)

status.description: Workflow lifecycle status (update). Publishing a version does not change it, so a workflow stays `draft` until this is set.

approved.description: Approval decision for approve_step; defaults to true

triggerType.description: Trigger type (create_trigger). Only `cron` and `event` can be created: a webhook trigger is system-managed and auto-created with the workflow (creating one is refused with WEBHOOK_TRIGGER_AUTO_MANAGED) — read its URL with `webhook_urls` instead.

triggerConfig.description: Trigger configuration (create_trigger, update_trigger). A `cron` trigger needs at least a `cronExpression` (`cron` is accepted as an alias) plus optional `timezone` (`tz` is accepted as an alias); an `event` trigger needs the event name it listens for. `name` labels the registration.

taskDecision.description: Human-task outcome (resolve_human_task); defaults to 'approved'. Use the outcome the authored node routes on — a `human` node routes on_approve/on_reject.

tools.name: platform_tools
tools.description: [Arch Build] Arch creates and changes projects, agents, tools, configuration, versions, and deployments. Manage tools within a project. Actions: list (paginated tools; use page and limit to retrieve later pages), get (tool detail), create (new tool), update (modify tool), delete (remove tool), test (execute tool test with input and optional timeoutMs). Note: tool CRUD routes through the Studio API. Destructive actions require user approval. Ordinary writes such as create, update, compile, and test require only a stable idempotencyKey. If the server returns MCP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED for a destructive action, ask the user conversationally and retry the identical call with the same idempotency key plus the returned confirmationRequestId and confirmationDecision:"approved". Never invent a request ID or confirmation grant.

toolId.description: Tool ID (for get, update, delete, test)

input.description: Input object for tool execution (for test); string values are passed unchanged

timeoutMs.description: Tool test timeout in milliseconds (for test)

type.description: Tool type (for create: http, sandbox, mcp, workflow, integration, searchai, table)

confirm.description: Set to true to confirm destructive operations (delete)

force.description: Delete the tool even when agents or workflows still reference it (delete). Without this the API returns 409 listing the consumers.
